title: Context-aware interruption snooze and runbook resumption
author: Priya Nair
description: Introduce a context-aware interruption 'snooze' flow plus a runbook resumption token so on-call engineers can safely defer noisy alerts while preserving ephemeral troubleshooting context. Motivation: recurring low-value interruptions during live debugging force responders to lose playbook state and trace anchors; we need an opt-in way to reduce noise without losing the captured context used to resume an investigation. This PR implements: 1) snooze manager with context fingerprinting: when an on-call user snoozes an alert via Slack or the web UI, the snooze attaches a lightweight context token that includes playbook id, active probe snapshot id, and optional KV anchors (sanitized). The token is encrypted with the cluster KMS and stored with a TTL. 2) deferred-checker: a background watcher that re-evaluates the underlying metric/alert conditions; if the metric crosses a configurable recovery delta, the snooze is auto-cancelled and escalation continues. 3) runbook resumptions: a safe resume API that accepts the token and rehydrates the ephemeral runbook workspace (playbook steps, last-queried telemetry snapshot, recent commands) into a temporary session for the user who created the snooze or a designated delegate. 4) guardrails: strict scope enforcement (tokens are single-use, bound to user id and repo/namespace), audit events for snooze/create/resume, and automatic expiry fallback to avoid stale claims. 5) UX: Slack quick action updates and a new compact 'Resume runbook' button in the incident web UI; both surface the token ID and expiration. 6) Feature flag and configuration: rollout is gated behind incident-bot.snooze_context.enabled=false by default and exposes recovery thresholds and permitted-scope lists via environment config. Implementation notes: added internal/snooze for core logic, telemetry/snapshotter to capture probe snapshots at snooze time, a minimal resume token codec (AES-GCM + KMS envelope) and server-side checks in the resume endpoint. Security review included KMS usage and audit logging; we restricted KV anchors to a redaction whitelist. Rollout plan: feature-flagged beta for 10% of teams, opt-in via console and Slack workspace deploy, monitor metrics: snooze-accepted rate, resume-success rate, unintended-escalation count. Testing: unit coverage for token lifecycle, e2e Slack flow test, integration test for deferred-checker including simulated metric recovery. Performance: background watcher runs in batches; an opt-in sampling mode prevents explosion of checks for high-cardinality signals. CI: initial flake observed in e2e auth test; re-ran and CI passed. Changelog/notes included. This PR is the foundation for a broader on-call ergonomics effort and is intentionally conservative in what it stores in tokens to avoid leaking sensitive payloads.

review_comments: Maya Chen: Nice end-to-end. Question: what prevents a delegate from resuming a token after the original owner leaves the org? Should we scope tokens to an expiry + allowed-delegates list?

Author (Priya): We scoped tokens to the creating user's id by default; delegates are allowed only when the creating user explicitly sets a delegate in the UI or when the team has a delegation rule in config. Added unit tests for delegate scoping.
Diego Alvarez: Deferred-checker batch loop looks like it could create a hot-loop under flapping signals. Can we add jitter and exponential backoff per signal?
Author (Priya): Added per-signal exponential backoff plus a global QPS cap and a sampling mode. Updated deferred_checker.go and added integration tests that simulate flapping metrics.
Aisha Gupta: audit entries are great, but ensure PII redaction for KV anchors. Are we using the redaction whitelist?
Author (Priya): Yes, token_codec.go enforces the redaction whitelist and we log sanitized anchors only. Security reviewed and approved.
release_notes: Add: context-aware snooze flow with runbook resumption token (opt-in behind incident-bot.snooze_context.enabled). Add: deferred-checker to auto-cancel snoozes on metric recovery. Improve: telemetry snapshot capture at snooze time. Fix: race in previous snooze expiry handler. Note: audit logging and KMS envelope used for token security.
